nodes.title: How to add an API endpoint
nodes.summary: Put the handler into the router that matches the audience (`routes/events.js` events for logged-in members, `routes/user.js` own account, `routes/admin.js` admin — auto-guarded), declare static paths before `/:id`, use the `firebaseAdmin.js` API, answer errors as `{ error: '<German text>' }`, write an audit log for admin mutations, call it from the SPA with the CSRF header, add a test in `test/devServer.test.js`, then update the wiki (`api-index` + router node) and run `npm run wiki`.

nodes.title: How to add a bot feature (helper, command, button)
nodes.summary: Discord-facing helpers live in `bot.js`, guarded by `isReady` and `try/catch`, are exported, and get a logging twin in `dev/mockBot.js` so mock mode and tests work. Slash commands are added in `registerSlashCommands` and handled in the `interactionCreate` dispatcher; buttons/modals use a prefixed custom id constant.

nodes.title: How to add a data collection
nodes.summary: Collections need no migration — just use a new name through the `firebaseAdmin.js` API. To keep tooling consistent, also add it to `SEED_COLLECTIONS` in `dev/seed.js` (so `npm run dev:reset` wipes it), optionally seed sample documents in `dev/seedData.js` (and update `EXPECTED_COUNTS` in `test/seed.test.js`), decide whether the admin system reset should wipe it, and document the shape in the data-model node.

nodes.title: How to add a field to events
nodes.summary: Event fields are whitelisted twice in `routes/admin.js` (create `baseEvent` and update `updates`) — add the field in both, add an input to the event wizard in `public/index.html`, read/write it in `editEvent()` and `saveEvent()` in `public/js/app.js`, display it where needed, give it a default in `dev/seedData.js#buildEvent`, and document it in the data-model node.

nodes.title: How to add a registration form field type
nodes.summary: A field type must exist in three places that mirror each other: `utils/formFields.js` (`FORM_FIELD_TYPE`), `bot.js` (Discord component in `applyFieldComponent`, parsing in `readModalField`) and `public/js/app.js` (`FORM_FIELD_TYPE_LABELS`, widget in `renderFormFields`/`initFormFieldWidgets`, value in `collectFormAnswers`). Answers must have the same format from web and Discord.

nodes.title: API index — every HTTP endpoint
nodes.summary: One line per endpoint with its guard and the node that documents it. Guards: `—` public, `U` logged-in user (`requireAuth`), `A` admin (`requireAuth` + `requireAdmin`). All mutating `/api/*` calls also need the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header.

nodes.title: System architecture
nodes.summary: DEMS is ONE Node.js process: an Express 5 server (REST API + static single-page app) and a discord.js bot that share one data layer — the Firestore client SDK, or a local SQLite adapter that mimics the same API when no Firebase config is set. The browser SPA (vanilla JS, Bootstrap, no build step) only talks to the REST API; Discord users only talk to the bot.

nodes.title: Authentication, session and CSRF
nodes.summary: Login is Discord OAuth2 only (or the persona login in dev mock mode). The result is a server-side `express-session` (stored in the database by `PersistentSessionStore`, 24 h cookie) holding `req.session.user = { id, username, displayName, avatar, roles, isAdmin, isNewUser }`. Admin = member has `DISCORD_ADMIN_ROLE_ID` at login time. The login checks a one-time OAuth `state` and starts a fresh session (`startUserSession`). Mutating `/api/*` and `/auth/*` requests (logout) need the per-session CSRF token in the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header.

nodes.title: bot.js — Discord bot and Discord helpers
nodes.summary: `bot.js` (~2200 lines) owns the discord.js `Client` and exports ~28 helpers the routes call (DMs, channel messages, roles, guild data, event channels, scheduled events, bot status/settings). It also handles all Discord interactions: `/events`, `/register`, `/unregister`, the "Anmelden" button + registration modal, and guest-invitation buttons. Every helper returns `false`/`[]`/`null` while the bot is not ready. Do not read it whole — jump by function name.

nodes.title: CI — GitLab pipeline and runner
nodes.summary: `.gitlab-ci.yml` runs `npm ci` + `npm test` in every pipeline (MRs, `main`, tags, branches without an open MR). The `docker-build` job builds the `runtime` and `dev` images and waits for the runtime HEALTHCHECK — always on `main` and tags, in MRs only when Docker or package files change. Jobs run on a self-hosted GitLab Runner next to GitLab (`ci/runner/`): an unprivileged runner for tests and a privileged Docker-in-Docker runner for jobs tagged `docker`.

nodes.title: Configuration — environment variables
nodes.summary: All configuration comes from environment variables (loaded from `.env` by dotenv; in Docker passed via `env_file`). Only `SESSION_SECRET` is strictly required to start; real use also needs the Discord app values, `DISCORD_GUILD_ID` and `BASE_URL`. `.env.example` lists everything.

nodes.title: Coding conventions
nodes.summary: CommonJS Node ≥22, no build step, no TypeScript. German for everything users see, English for code, comments and docs. Data access only through `firebaseAdmin.js`; every route handler has its own `try/catch` and answers `{ error: '<German>' }`. Tests with `node:test`, written first. English imperative commit messages, German PR descriptions.

nodes.title: Data layer — firebaseAdmin.js and the SQLite adapter
nodes.summary: All persistence goes through `firebaseAdmin.js`, which exports a subset of the Firestore modular API (`db, collection, doc, getDoc, getDocs, addDoc, setDoc, updateDoc, deleteDoc, query, where, orderBy, writeBatch`). With all six `FIREBASE_*` variables set it is real Firestore (client SDK); with none set it is `db/sqliteAdapter.js`, a JSON document store in one SQLite table that mimics the same API. Partially set → startup error.

nodes.title: Data model — collections and document shapes
nodes.summary: Eleven schemaless collections. `events`, `registrations`, `comments`, `auditLogs`, `polls` use auto ids; `pollVotes` uses `<pollId>_<userId>`; `users` uses the Discord user id; `botMessages/templates`, `botSettings/config`, `maintenanceSettings/config` are singleton documents; `devMeta/seed` exists only in dev mock mode. All dates are ISO-8601 strings. Shapes are defined by the code that writes them (no schema file) — the producers are listed per collection.

nodes.title: Date polls — finding a date with "passt" / "wenn nötig"
nodes.summary: Admins propose 2–10 dates (`polls`), members vote per date with "passt" or "wenn nötig" (admins can rename the three answers per poll) on the web or through a Discord button with two prefilled selects (`pollVotes`, one document per member). The posted Discord message shows the tally live. A scheduler closes polls after their deadline and DMs the creator; "Event erstellen" opens the event wizard prefilled and `POST /api/admin/events` with `fromPoll` decides the poll and DMs every voter.

nodes.title: Decision log — specs, plans, audits
nodes.summary: Chronological list of the design decisions that shaped DEMS, with links to the full spec/plan/audit documents. Read the linked document only when you change that area; this page gives the one-line rationale.

nodes.title: Deployment — VPS with Docker (Hostinger + Traefik example)
nodes.summary: Run the private image `moritakahashi/dems` (or build from source) with a compose file that passes `.env` into the container (`env_file`), keeps SQLite on a volume and sits behind a TLS reverse proxy. On a Hostinger VPS the Docker Manager stores projects under `/docker/<project>/` and Traefik routes `*.hstgr.cloud` hosts via container labels.

nodes.title: Dev mock mode (dev/) — run without Discord and Firebase
nodes.summary: `npm run dev:mock` (or `docker compose -f compose.dev.yaml up --build`) starts DEMS with `DEV_MOCK=true`: a separate SQLite file with seeded dummy data, a persona login instead of Discord OAuth, and a simulated Discord server whose actions are logged as `[MOCK-DISCORD]`. It refuses to start with `NODE_ENV=production`.

nodes.title: Directory map and reading strategy
nodes.summary: Where every file lives, how big it is and how to read it cheaply. Four files hold most of the tokens (`public/js/app.js`, `public/css/style.css`, `bot.js`, `public/index.html`) — never read them whole; jump via the function/section maps in their wiki nodes and `grep -n`.

nodes.title: Discord integration — what DEMS does in Discord
nodes.summary: The bot announces events (embed + "Anmelden"/"Zum Event" buttons), lets members register through a modal, offers `/events`, `/register`, `/unregister`, sends DMs for every registration change, assigns/removes an event role, optionally creates private voice/text channels per event, and can create native Discord scheduled events. Everything targets ONE guild (`DISCORD_GUILD_ID`).

nodes.title: Docker — image, stages, compose files
nodes.summary: Multi-stage `Dockerfile` on `node:24-bookworm-slim`: `runtime` (default, production: non-root `node` user, `NODE_ENV=production`, SQLite on volume `/app/data`, healthcheck `GET /healthz`) and `dev` (all deps, nodemon polling, used by `compose.dev.yaml`). `compose.yaml` runs production from `.env`; `compose.dev.yaml` runs the dev mock mode with the source bind-mounted.

nodes.title: Event lifecycle — status, series, check-in
nodes.summary: Events have four statuses: `draft` → `active` → `archived`, plus `cancelled`. Only `active` events are listed publicly and accept registrations. Admins create/edit through a 5-step wizard; recurring events are stored as independent instances sharing a `seriesId`. Check-in uses a 6-digit code the admin generates and members type in on the event page.

nodes.title: Registration form fields — types, web widgets, Discord components
nodes.summary: An event's `formFields` is a list of `{ label, type, required, options[], description }`. Eight types exist (`text`, `textarea`, `dropdown`, `checkbox`, `user`, `role`, `channel`, `mentionable`); each maps to a web widget and a Discord modal component. Answers are stored in `registration.formAnswers` keyed by the label, in the same format from web and Discord. Forms with more than 5 fields are web-only.

nodes.title: public/js/app.js — SPA logic and function map
nodes.summary: One ~4550-line vanilla-JS file with global functions and globals (no modules, no build). A hash router (`handleRoute`) shows one `<section class="app-section">` at a time; every section has a `show*Section()` loader that fetches the REST API and renders HTML strings. Never read the file whole: find the function below, then `grep -n "function <name>" public/js/app.js` and read ~80 lines from there.

nodes.title: public/index.html and public/css/style.css — markup and styling map
nodes.summary: `index.html` (~1760 lines) contains every section and modal statically; JS toggles `display`. `style.css` (~3270 lines) is a dark theme driven by CSS variables in `:root`, organised in banner-commented blocks. Find things by element id (HTML) or block header (CSS) with `grep -n`.

nodes.title: Glossary — German UI terms and code names
nodes.summary: The UI, API errors and Discord messages are German; code and data use English names. This table maps the German term a user or ticket uses to the field, status or function in the code.

nodes.title: DEMS wiki — entry point
nodes.summary: Knowledge graph of the DEMS codebase for coding agents and humans. Each page is a node with frontmatter (id, type, tags, sources, typed edges) and a one-line TL;DR; `graph.json` holds all nodes, summaries and edges for cheap retrieval. Start here, pick the smallest set of nodes for your task, then open source files at the given grep anchors.

nodes.title: Known issues and pitfalls
nodes.summary: Verified bugs and traps in the current code (2026-10-02), each with location and impact. Check this list before debugging "weird" behaviour; when you fix one, delete its row and update the linked node.

nodes.title: landing/ — standalone marketing page
nodes.summary: `landing/` is a separate static marketing website for DEMS (hero, features, screenshot gallery, security, tech stack, config, beta access). It is NOT served by `server.js` (which only serves `public/`) and is excluded from the Docker image. Ignore it for app work.

nodes.title: Maintenance mode and panic mode
nodes.summary: One settings document, `maintenanceSettings/config`, drives four admin switches: warning banner, planned-maintenance banner, "login disabled" (non-admins) and "registrations disabled". Panic mode is an emergency lockdown that turns all of them on at once; it can be switched on without a password but only switched off with `ADMIN_RESET_PASSWORD`. Admins are never locked out.

nodes.title: middleware/ — auth guards, maintenance gates, validators
nodes.summary: Three small modules. `auth.js` exports `requireAuth` / `requireAdmin` (session-based, 401/403 JSON) plus `safeEqual` (constant-time secret compare) and the login helpers `createCsrfToken` and `startUserSession`. `maintenance.js` exports `isRegistrationBlocked`, `getLoginBlockReason` and the `checkRegistrationAllowed` middleware (503). `validators.js` exports `validateEvent`, `validateRegStatus`, `validateBotMessages` (400 with German messages).

nodes.title: Registration flow — rules, statuses, waitlist, guests
nodes.summary: Every registration (web or Discord) goes through `registerUserForEvent()` in `utils/registrationService.js`. It checks event status, duplicates, role requirement, guest permission and required form fields, then decides the status (slot events: main role, else first free fallback role, else waitlist): `waitlisted` when capacity (incl. guests) is exceeded, otherwise `accepted` (instant approval) or `pending` (manual). Admins move registrations between statuses; freed places promote the oldest waitlisted registration that fits.

nodes.title: Reminders, start notifications and bot presence
nodes.summary: `startReminderScheduler()` runs `checkReminders()` every 5 minutes: for each active event it DMs accepted participants when a configured reminder time (`reminderHours[].hours` before start) is reached, and once when the event starts. Duplicates are prevented only by flags stored in the event (`reminderHours[].sent`, `eventStartNotificationSent`), written before the DMs go out. Bot presence (status + activity text with live variables) comes from `botSettings/config` and is applied on ready, on save, and every 5 minutes if `autoUpdatePresence` is on.

nodes.title: Request lifecycle (middleware order)
nodes.summary: Every HTTP request passes `server.js` middleware in this exact order: healthz → helmet → cors → rate limits → body parsers → session → CSRF → static files → (debug log) → routers → misc endpoints → SPA fallback. Mutating `/api/*` calls need the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header; everything unknown returns `index.html`.

nodes.title: Role slots — line-ups with main and fallback roles
nodes.summary: An event can define up to 10 slots (`{ id, name, emoji, capacity }`, e.g. Tank 2 / Heiler 3 / Schaden 10). Members pick a main role plus optional fallback roles; `registerUserForEvent` gives them the main role, else the first free fallback (slot order), else the waitlist. Freed places go to the oldest waitlist entry that wants that slot. Every change refreshes the stored Discord announcements (debounced 2 s); all place-changing work runs under an in-memory lock per event.

nodes.title: routes/admin.js — admin API
nodes.summary: Mounted at `/api/admin`; every route requires `requireAuth` + `requireAdmin` (`router.use` at the top). Covers event CRUD and lifecycle, registration review, CSV export, Discord announce/sync/import, bot message templates, audit log, full system reset, bot control center and maintenance/panic mode. Most mutations write an audit log entry via `addAuditLog`.

nodes.title: routes/auth.js — Discord OAuth2 login
nodes.summary: Mounted at `/auth`. `/auth/discord` redirects to Discord OAuth2 (scopes `identify guilds guilds.members.read`) with a one-time `state` kept in the session; `/auth/discord/callback` exchanges the code, checks guild membership and admin role, applies the maintenance login block, upserts the `users` document and stores the session user; `/auth/me` returns the session user; `POST /auth/logout` (CSRF token) destroys the session.

nodes.title: routes/events.js — event endpoints for logged-in members
nodes.summary: Mounted at `/api/events`. Every route needs a login (`router.use(requireAuth)`, no public preview); `router.param('id')` answers 404 to non-admins for `draft`/`archived` events on every `/:id` route. Lists and reads events, and lets members register/unregister, check in with a code, see participants and write comments. Registration logic itself lives in `utils/registrationService.js`.

nodes.title: routes/polls.js — member API for date polls
nodes.summary: Mounted at `/api/polls`, every route needs a logged-in member. Lists polls with the own vote status, returns one poll with tally and own vote, and stores a vote (`PUT /:id/vote`, blocked during maintenance). Admin routes for polls live in `routes/admin.js`.

nodes.title: routes/user.js — profile, badges, settings, account
nodes.summary: Mounted at `/api/user`, every route needs a logged-in user. Provides the user's registrations, a profile with stats and computed badges, a user search for guest invitations, the `acceptInvitations` setting and full account deletion.

nodes.title: How to run and debug DEMS locally
nodes.summary: Fastest path: `npm install && npm run dev:mock` → http://localhost:3000 → "Mit Discord anmelden" → pick a persona. Real Discord: fill `.env`, `npm run dev`. Add `DEBUG_MODE=true` for request/DB/bot traces and the `#debug` styling guide. `npm run dev:reset` restores the dummy data.

nodes.title: Security model and open audit findings
nodes.summary: Defenses: helmet CSP (scripts, styles and fonts only from `'self'`, still allows `unsafe-inline`), CORS to `BASE_URL`, rate limits, double-submit CSRF on `/api` and `/auth`, httpOnly session cookie, server-side admin guards, `escapeHtml` + DOMPurify in the SPA. The 2026-04-22 audit lists 28 findings; most are still open — check the table before touching auth, events or exports. Serve DEMS over HTTPS: helmet's default `upgrade-insecure-requests` breaks plain-HTTP access from anything but localhost.

nodes.title: server.js — Express app, misc endpoints, startup
nodes.summary: `server.js` builds the Express 5 app (security headers, rate limits, session, CSRF, static files), mounts the four routers, defines five small endpoints itself (`/healthz`, `/api/csrf-token`, `/api/maintenance/status`, `/api/server-info`, `/api/updates`) plus the SPA fallback, then starts the HTTP server, the Discord bot and the reminder scheduler.

nodes.title: Testing — node:test suites and helpers
nodes.summary: `npm test` runs `node --test "test/**/*.test.js"` (built-in runner, no dependencies). Server behaviour is tested end-to-end by spawning `server.js` / `dev/start.js` in a child process with a temp SQLite file and driving it with a cookie-aware fetch client that handles CSRF. Single frontend functions run in `node:vm` against a fake DOM (`loadFrontendApp`). Browser smoke tests (Playwright, Chromium only) run separately with `npm run test:e2e`.

nodes.title: utils/ — domain helpers
nodes.summary: Shared domain logic used by routes and the bot: `registrationService.js` (the single source of truth for creating registrations), `formFields.js` (field types and answer format), `eventUtils.js` (loading registrations/line-ups, waitlist promotion, audit log), `capacity.js` and `slotService.js` (pure place and slot rules), `eventLock.js` (per-event lock), `announcementRefresh.js` (debounced live announcements), `eventUrl.js` (links to event pages), `userProfile.js` (users upsert after login) and `debugLog.js` (`DEBUG_MODE` logger).
